selected_mechanisms.root_cause: updateTssAndConnectorAddresses can be called by tssAddressUpdater OR tssAddress and reassigns connectorAddress to any address, granting full mint/burn capability with no on-chain timelock, no enforced multi-sig threshold, no delay. A single TSS key compromise = full token supply control.
selected_mechanisms.attacker_model: Attacker who compromised tssAddress (validator set) or tssAddressUpdater. On-chain it is a single address with full power (multi-sig is off-chain).
selected_mechanisms.exploit_path: 1. compromise tssAddress/tssAddressUpdater. 2. updateTssAndConnectorAddresses(attacker, malicious_connector). 3. malicious_connector.mint(attacker, MAX) — unbounded ZETA. 4. dump for other assets, draining value.
selected_mechanisms.who_loses: All ZETA holders (inflation destroys value); bridge users (burned tokens unbacked).
selected_mechanisms.who_gains: Attacker gains newly minted ZETA redeemable for protocol/LP assets.
selected_mechanisms.why_carried: Privileged precondition (TSS compromise) but on-chain zero defense: no timelock/multisig/delay. Single-key risk for a cross-chain bridge token is a genuine architectural finding.

selected_mechanisms.root_cause: connectorAddress not set in constructor, defaults address(0). mint/burn guards (msg.sender != connectorAddress) make the functions un-callable (DoS) in the deployment window; if connectorAddress were ever set to address(0) again it would permanently DoS mint/burn (updateTssAndConnectorAddresses' zero-check prevents this).
selected_mechanisms.exploit_path: 1. deploy ZetaNonEth, connectorAddress=address(0). 2. before updateTssAndConnectorAddresses, no cross-chain mint/burn possible — bridge DoS'd.
selected_mechanisms.who_loses: Bridge users unable to complete cross-chain transfers during uninitialized window.
selected_mechanisms.why_carried: Deployment-window DoS — bounded/temporary but real unavailability; Medium.

unresolved_mechanisms.mechanism: missing supply cap — mint() applies no upper bound; connector (legit or compromised) can mint MAX in one call
unresolved_mechanisms.source_evidence: mint() calls _mint(mintee, value) with no cap; value caller-supplied uint256.
unresolved_mechanisms.unresolved_question: Whether the connector enforces a supply cap/mint bound — not in this file.

rejected_mechanisms.rejecting_source_fact: OZ ERC20._mint makes no external calls (no ERC-777 hook); state updated atomically.
rejected_mechanisms.why_unexploitable: No external call returning control during _mint.

rejected_mechanisms.rejecting_source_fact: burnFrom decrements caller allowance before burning; connector must hold allowance; only connector can call.

impact_direction.attacker_receives: Unbounded ZETA (if TSS key compromised and malicious connector set) or denial of cross-chain service (deployment/DoS).
impact_direction.attacker_preserves: Control over bridge token supply if TSS key held.
impact_direction.victim_loses: All ZETA holders lose value via inflation; bridge users lose cross-chain capability during DoS.
impact_direction.invariant_violated: Cross-chain mint/burn authorization correctness: connector-gating bypassed if connectorAddress updated to attacker; supply correctness violated by unbounded mint.
impact_direction.not_self_funded_or_dust_or_admin_or_timi: TSS-compromise path privileged (HIGH not CRITICAL) but impact protocol-wide token inflation; not self-funded/dust; TSS is a realistic compromise target. Deployment-window DoS permissionless (Medium).
